answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through a bond locked in a public contract: each new identity must stake scarce tokens, and disputes can slash the stake when signed task evidence shows fraud. Splitting one agent into a hundred names does not multiply its influence for free; every name ties up capital and risks forfeiture. A meadow of identities may look like a gale of activity, but sable accounts still need independent bonds, making Sybil attacks costly rather than merely numerous.
